title: Incremental, Marginal and Component VaR

maps.tested: Marked Very Important by the sheet and named by five recall sources. Used both as a computation and as the input to an allocation decision.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'calculate incremental VaR of including platinum asset in the silver asset', a two-asset incremental setup; 'allocation using MVaR'; 'MVaR, vol, rf is given: calculate Sharpe ratio', which chains marginal VaR into a performance measure. Closed-book: marginal VaR = (VaR/P) x beta; component VaR = individual VaR x rho. Shortcut to find: when ranking marginal VaRs, only beta matters. The intermediate-result trap between marginal and component VaR is explicitly in GARP's repertoire.

vardeezReading: IM-5: Very Important; his pointers are marginal, incremental and component VaR calculations, and diversified vs undiversified VaR.

los.vardeez: Marginal, incremental and component VaR calculations; diversified vs undiversified VaR

selectors.name: Incremental VaR of adding a position
selectors.what: Incremental VaR of including a platinum position in a silver book: the full revaluation VaR(p+a) - VaR(p), against the marginal VaR shortcut (marginal VaR x amount added). A position as large as the book needs the full revaluation.
selectors.theory: Incremental VaR is the before-and-after change in VaR owing to a new position; a fall means the trade is a hedge. It differs from marginal VaR because a large trade changes VaR nonlinearly; the shortcut ignores second-order terms, is good only for small trades and allows real-time limits.

selectors.name: Allocation using marginal VaR
selectors.what: Which position to cut or add to, or which to grow for a better return-to-risk trade-off, using marginal VaRs: cut the largest marginal VaR, add to the lowest; for return to risk, grow the position with the highest E_i / marginal VaR_i using excess returns.
selectors.theory: Minimum risk is reached when all marginal VaRs (all betas) are equal; maximum return to risk when E_i / marginal VaR_i, equivalently E_i / beta_i, is constant (a restatement of the CAPM).

selectors.name: Marginal VaR chained into Sharpe ratio
selectors.what: Given marginal VaRs, weights, volatility and the risk-free rate, back out portfolio sigma (VaR/W = sum of w_i x marginal VaR_i, sigma_p = (VaR/W)/alpha) and compute the Sharpe ratio = (expected return - rf) / sigma_p.
selectors.theory: Weighted marginal VaRs sum to VaR/W by Euler's theorem, so portfolio volatility can be recovered from them; the Sharpe ratio is excess return over that volatility.

selectors.name: Marginal and component VaR formulas
selectors.what: Closed-book formulas: marginal VaR = (VaR/W) x beta_i; component VaR = marginal VaR x position = individual VaR x rho_i = VaR x w_i x beta_i; components sum to portfolio VaR.
selectors.theory: Marginal VaR is the change in portfolio VaR from an extra dollar of exposure (unitless, proportional to beta); component VaR is a currency partition of portfolio VaR, summing exactly to it, with negative components acting as hedges.

selectors.name: Ranking marginal VaRs needs only beta
selectors.what: When asked to rank positions by marginal VaR (for example to choose which to cut), only the betas matter, since marginal VaR = (VaR/W) x beta_i and the factor is common to all positions.

selectors.name: Trap: marginal VaR versus component VaR
selectors.what: The stem asks for component VaR but the marginal VaR (a unitless figure, or money amount mistaken for it) or the individual VaR sits among the options, or the reverse; also the tangent (component VaR) against the curve (incremental VaR) when a position is deleted.

selectors.name: Diversified versus undiversified VaR
selectors.what: Diversified (portfolio) VaR against undiversified VaR, the sum of individual VaRs (individual VaR = alpha x sigma_i x |position|); the diversification benefit is the difference, and undiversified equals diversified only when all correlations are one with no short positions.
selectors.theory: Diversified VaR takes correlations between components into account; individual VaR ignores them, so the sum of individual VaRs is an upper bound when positions are long.

notSelected: IM-5 b (impact of correlation on portfolio risk, beyond its role in diversified versus undiversified VaR) and IM-5 e (risk management versus portfolio management) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; the best-hedge position formula, simulation-based component VaR and the Barings and tracking-error report examples are not selected.
